title: HTML image maps with map and area
learningObjectives: Explain html image maps with map and area and its role in modern HTML.
Select the correct elements, attributes, APIs, or browser behaviour for a practical use case.
Distinguish current practices from obsolete, limited, or legacy techniques.
Build and inspect a working example while considering accessibility and maintainability.
Diagnose common implementation errors and explain the trade-offs of the chosen approach.

understand.concept: An image map makes different regions of one image act as separate links or actions. The img element names the map with usemap; a map element supplies a name; area elements define clickable shapes such as rect, circle, or poly with coordinates, href, and alternative text. Coordinates are measured against the rendered image's intrinsic coordinate system, so responsive scaling requires careful handling or a different interaction pattern. Every interactive region needs a meaningful accessible name, and the image needs suitable alternative text.
understand.whyItMatters: Image maps are useful for diagrams, plans, and illustrations where regions correspond to distinct destinations. They are less flexible than ordinary links and can become difficult to maintain when images resize or change.
understand.analogy: A map image is a printed floor plan with invisible clickable zones drawn over rooms.
understand.analogyLimit: Unlike a printed plan, browser hit regions have exact coordinate rules and must also work for keyboard and assistive-technology users.

explain.narrative: Create one map image with rectangular, circular, and polygon regions. Inspect how coordinates identify each region and why the alt text on each area describes its destination rather than its shape.

examples.explanation: The image references a named map. The rectangular and circular areas link to different pages and provide destination-specific alternative text.
examples.expectedOutput: A campus map image with clickable library and computer-lab regions; the image file must exist.

examples.explanation: A polygon is defined by successive x,y coordinate pairs. Keep the coordinate data synchronized with the source image.
examples.expectedOutput: The polygon region links to the northern-region page.

practise.guidedTask: Create an image map for a supplied diagram with at least two rectangular areas and one circular area. Give every area a useful alt description and test each destination.
practise.independentTask: Make the map usable at narrow viewport widths. If the coordinate mapping cannot remain accurate and accessible, replace it with a responsive image plus a visible list of ordinary links.
hints: Coordinates are relative to the image's intrinsic dimensions, not arbitrary CSS pixels.
The usemap value references the map name with a leading #.
Do not use vague area text such as 'click here'; name the destination or action.

questions.prompt: Which attribute connects an img element to a map?
questions.explanation: The usemap attribute references the map by its fragment identifier.

questions.prompt: Which element defines clickable regions in an image map?
questions.explanation: Each area element describes one interactive region.

questions.prompt: Which shape uses four coordinate values for its bounding corners?
questions.explanation: A rectangle uses left, top, right, and bottom coordinates.

questions.prompt: Why can responsive resizing break a basic image map?
options: The area coordinates may no longer align with the scaled image
The map element becomes a CSS stylesheet
The href attribute changes to a number
questions.answer: The area coordinates may no longer align with the scaled image
questions.explanation: Coordinates are defined against the image coordinate space; scaling must be accounted for.

questions.prompt: What should an interactive area provide?
options: A meaningful alt text describing its destination or action
An empty alt value in every case
questions.answer: A meaningful alt text describing its destination or action
questions.explanation: The area needs an accessible name that communicates its purpose.
